scope: G6 measured IFC notifier-context binding barrier; native06 full acceptance and a post-change native timing comparison remain open.
change: IFC-class DMA_NOTIFY rebinding can retain queued draws when its real four-byte GROBJ RAMIN writeback is disjoint from every pending output and read-only attachment guard. It still reads/validates the original binding handle, updates notify_context, writes GROBJ word1 and updates hardware mirrors. Actual notifications and RAMIN aliases retain barriers.
validation: RED: observed disjoint binding incorrectly returns barrier=true before change
Complete real WebGPU regression: real binding, GROBJ/mirror values and two successive draws preserve blend history with one batch/readback
Both output and read-only guard aliases at the four-byte RAMIN writeback retain barriers
Invalid instance and invalid notification handle retain conservative ordering before a PGRAPH fault
Existing FIFO/device graph notifier regressions pass
limits: No notification, fence or query is synthesized, skipped or completed early.
This preserves ordering for the binding writeback; other IFC operations retain their existing checked footprints.
Native performance improvement and resolution of06 timeout are not inferred from the profile or unit tests.
